issues.description: changedFiles comparison uses absolute paths against relative paths from VitestGit
issues.detail: isIncluded() runs pm.isMatch on absolute paths (after slash+cleanUrl) and then checks `this.changedFiles.includes(filename)`. VitestGit.findChangedFiles typically returns paths relative to the git root, so the includes() check will silently never match unless paths are normalized. Either resolve changedFiles to absolute paths in onTestRunStart or normalize both sides. Show the test that proves a non-trivial repo layout (root != git root) actually works.

issues.description: Stale changedFiles state across reruns in watch mode
issues.detail: changedFiles is set in onTestRunStart but never reset when options.changed is falsy on a subsequent run, and globCache is only cleared when changedFiles is set, not when it transitions back to undefined. In watch mode with config reload this leaves a stale filter and a poisoned cache. Reset changedFiles to undefined and clear the cache unconditionally at run start.

issues.description: Silent fallback when git resolution fails hides a real failure mode
issues.detail: findChangedFiles can return null (not a git repo, bad ref, git missing). The code coerces to undefined and proceeds as if no filter were requested, so the user asked for changed-only coverage and silently got full coverage instead. That's the worst kind of bug: looks like it worked. Fail loud, or at minimum warn with the resolved ref.

issues.description: CLI transform accepts boolean inputs that argv parsing will never deliver
issues.detail: The transform branches on `value === true` and `value === false`, but CLI arg values arrive as strings. Either it's dead code or it papers over a typing lie elsewhere. Pick one: handle strings only, or document why a boolean shows up here. Don't ship both.

issues.description: Three concerns landed in one patch
issues.detail: This diff adds a new coverage option, introduces a new CoverageProvider lifecycle hook (onTestRunStart wired into three call sites in core.ts), and changes isIncluded to apply cleanUrl to every filename. The cleanUrl change in particular is a behavioral fix that affects all users regardless of the new option and deserves its own commit with its own test rationale. Bisect-hostile as submitted.

issues.description: No test exercises the actual git path; all coverage tests use changed:'HEAD' against the working tree
issues.detail: Every new test passes `changed: 'HEAD'` and relies on uncommitted fixture state. None exercises a real ref like a branch or tag through VitestGit for the coverage.changed code path (the v0.0.1 test sets test.changed, not coverage.changed). The path-normalization bug above would not be caught by anything here. Add a test that resolves a non-HEAD ref via coverage.changed end-to-end.

review.summary: The feature is useful and the shape is roughly right, but the patch ships three changes glued together and has a path-normalization bug that the tests don't catch. changedFiles is compared via Array.includes against strings that have been through slash+cleanUrl while VitestGit returns git-relative paths — that's a silent miss waiting to happen. Watch-mode state isn't reset between runs, and a failed git resolution silently degrades to full coverage instead of erroring. Split the cleanUrl fix and the onTestRunStart hook into their own commits, normalize paths on both sides of the changedFiles check with a test that proves it, and fail loud when git can't resolve the ref. NEEDS-WORK.
